title: How Many Calories Do Women Need a Day to Lose Weight?
intro: Many working women can lose weight on an estimated 1,300 to 1,700 calories a day, depending on body size and activity. Use that as a starting point, then adjust based on your progress.

sections.h: Why there's no one number for everyone
sections.p: A 50 kg woman who works from home needs less energy than a 75 kg woman who does field work. Age, height, muscle and daily movement all play a part. So all these numbers are estimates only.

Multiply your body weight (kg) by 28. That's the estimated calories to maintain your weight. Subtract 300-500 calories to lose weight slowly. Example: 65 kg x 28 = 1,820, minus 400 = an estimated 1,420 calories a day.

Avoid eating below an estimated 1,200 calories a day without professional guidance. Going too low makes you hungry, tired and hard to focus at work. A realistic target is around 0.5-1 kg a week, and even slower is okay.

A teh tarik can reach an estimated 150-200 calories a glass. Meeting kuih is an estimated 100-200 calories per piece. Roti canai with curry is around 300-400 calories. No need to avoid them, just be aware and count them too.

When you cut calories, protein helps you feel full and protects your muscle. Try to have protein at every meal, for example eggs, chicken, fish, tauhu or tempe. A piece of chicken the size of your palm is already good.

action: Calculate your estimated calories using the formula weight x 28 minus 400.
Record what you eat for 3 days, including drinks and meeting kuih.
Make sure every meal has one protein source.
Weigh yourself 2-3 times a week and look at the average after 2-3 weeks before changing your calories.
myth: Many think the less you eat, the faster you'll slim down. In reality, eating too little often makes you extremely hungry, lose muscle and end up overeating again.

faq.q: Do I need to count calories forever?
faq.a: No. Count for a few weeks so you get to know portions. After that, many people can just use hand and plate estimates.

faq.q: I have thyroid problems or PCOS. Is this formula suitable?
faq.a: These conditions can affect weight and energy. Please check with your doctor first before setting a calorie target.

faq.q: If I'm pregnant, can I cut calories?
faq.a: During pregnancy, don't go on a calorie deficit on your own. Discuss suitable nutrition and weight gain with your doctor.
